curriculum.lesson_evidence: Reciting a poem uses memorised or lightly cued text, paced breathing at line breaks and restrained gesture that supports meaning. Practise looking up at listeners during stable lines.

lesson.child_mission: Reciting a poem uses memorised or lightly cued text, paced breathing at line breaks and restrained gesture that supports meaning. Practise looking up at listeners during stable lines.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mark two breath points and one emphasis word on a short poem you will recite.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Breath at structural breaks; emphasis matches meaning climax.

CHECK
Acting out every line with big gestures. Restraint usually serves poetry better.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Recite a short poem (own or approved) with marked breaths; reflect on pace and one audience response.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Recite a short poem (own or approved) with marked breaths; reflect on pace and one audience response. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using recitation on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Acting out every line with big gestures.. Correction: Strong answer: Breath at structural breaks;. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Acting out every line with big gestures. Restraint usually serves poetry better. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating recitation on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with recitation, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about recitation with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for recitation. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

Reciting a poem uses memorised or lightly cued text, paced breathing at line breaks and restrained gesture that supports meaning. Practise looking up at listeners during stable lines.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided.
